customManagers.description: Talos version in versions.env -- the ONLY place this is tracked now. A Kustomize `replacements` block (config/kustomization.yaml) projects this into every SUC Plan's spec.version and talosctl image tag at build time, so there is no longer a separate manager for those; bumping this file is the whole update. The Factory installer tag in the machine configs (below) is the one pin Kustomize cannot reach and still needs its own manager. A bump here does NOT require regenerating SCHEMATIC_ID: the schematic ID is a content hash of the extension list and is independent of the Talos version -- the same ID serves v1.12.0 through v1.13.9. Only editing schematic.yaml changes it. The talos group is still never auto-merged, for the real reasons: the upgrade reboots nodes, and the Image Factory builds per (schematic, version) pair, so a brand-new release may have no image for these extensions yet. The Talos image workflow checks both.

Kubernetes control-plane/kubelet version in versions.env, upgraded independently of TALOS_VERSION via talosctl upgrade-k8s (plans/talos-kubernetes-upgrade.yaml). Grouped separately from talos and never auto-merged for the same reasons: the upgrade touches every node's control-plane components, and the Talos image workflow checks it is within Talos's supported skew for TALOS_VERSION.

Factory installer tag in the machine configs. Decides which Talos a rebuilt node installs, so leaving it behind versions.env means a rebuild lands on the old version and needs an immediate upgrade. This is the one pin Kustomize's replacements cannot reach: Talos machine config is applied by hand via talosctl, entirely outside Kustomize/Flux. The SCHEMATIC_ID in the same string is NOT tracked and must still be regenerated by hand whenever the schematic changes.

packageRules.description: Group all Talos ecosystem updates into one PR. talosctl is no longer tracked separately -- its image tag is now the same Kustomize-replacements field as TALOS_VERSION (see config/kustomization.yaml), so it cannot drift from it the way it used to and needs no manager of its own.
Kubernetes control-plane version -- tracked and upgraded independently of Talos, never auto-merged (control-plane component upgrade).
Label major updates — CI workflow uses this to skip Trivy auto-merge
Label minor/patch updates — CI Trivy gate evaluates auto-merge eligibility
Disable digest updates for Talos images
Route all patch updates through Trivy gate (no Renovate-side automerge)
